quotes.text: As policymakers, we have a responsibility to ensure AI is developed and used responsibly, with appropriate oversight and commonsense guardrails. I appreciated the opportunity to hear directly from Pope Leo XIV and engage with fellow legislators on one of the defining challenges of our time.

This morning, I was pleased to meet with @UTSA President Taylor Eighmy.
 
We discussed the groundbreaking work UTSA is doing in the artificial intelligence and cybersecurity fields. I look forward to working together to ensure the next generation of researchers are from Texas! https://t.co/ZUzPnDzQTu

Great news for TAMIU! The National Science Foundation announced $200,000 for TAMIU to improve student artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm development.

These federal dollars will be used to enhance statistics curricula, the backbone of AI algorithms, for engineering and math students at TAMIU. This will help equip students with the necessary foundation to apply their statistical skills to real-world AI projects.

Congratulations! The jobs of tomorrow are being created right here in South Texas.

Today, I announced $799,853 in federal grant funding for TAMIU.

The funding consists of three separate awards for the establishment of a center for physics-based AI application training, enhancement of statistics curricula for AI development, and STEM recruitment.

These grants will help ensure TAMIU students are ready for the jobs of tomorrow.

Today, I met with Texas Southern University President James W. Crawford III.

We discussed how AI can be used to ensure the success of students.

In Congress, I will continue to fight for resources that expand educational opportunities for our students.

Today, I attended the Congressional Showcase of the National Artificial Intelligence Research Institute.

We discussed the importance of education in Artificial Intelligence and the potential benefits it offers to the American people. I met with my daughter Christina, Kerry Kinirons, and Dr. Jason O'Kane, who were presenting from Texas A&M, as they discussed their innovative summer programs focused on AI.

I'd like to thank the National Science Foundation and Texas A&M for their commitment to advancing our nation through technological and scientific breakthroughs like these.

Earlier today, I met with Bart Riesing, Matt Lake, and Lucas Hoffmann from HavocAI. We delved into their groundbreaking work integrating Artificial Intelligence with defense systems and explored the potential future applications of this technology across our service branches. I look forward to continued collaboration with them in the future!

I'm pleased that the TAKE IT DOWN Act passed in the House, after passing in the Senate with strong bipartisan support.

As a father, husband, and South Texan, I was proud to cosponsor this important bill to remove harmful deepfake content, protect victims, and hold bad actors accountable online. I look forward to it being signed into law without delay.
https://t.co/WScTWkl1e3

I was proud to cosponsor the Take It Down Act and I’m pleased to see this critical, bipartisan bill signed into law. I thank my colleagues @SenTedCruz and @RepMariaSalazar for their leadership in getting it across the finish line.

Let me be clear: no child - from Texas or anywhere in the world - should fall victim to AI-generated abuse. As technology evolves, I’m committed to ensuring our laws evolve with it.

Read more in @TexasTribune.⬇️

Let me be clear: no child, from Texas or anywhere in the world, should fall victim to AI-generated abuse. Thanks to this law, families and individuals will finally have a way to demand action and accountability online.

Congress must lead on AI regulation. In a digital age, we cannot ignore the technologies that touch every part of our lives.

But taking away states' ability to regulate AI is the wrong approach.

We need smart, balanced federal standards, not one-size-fits-all rules buried in a budget bill.

I'm excited to share another important win for South Texas in this year's Homeland Security appropriations bill. I helped secure $300 million for Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII) technology, including procuring and deploying new detection devices, AI and Machine learning capabilities, as well as  IT infrastructure.

This investment is vital because it speeds up legal trade, strengthens contraband detection, and keeps dangerous items out of our communities. I’ll keep working to modernize our ports and enhance border safety.

Today, I met with Daniela Beckelhymer, a Laredo native, and Jose Colchadoromero during #MathSciOnTheHill 2026 Advocacy Day. We discussed the importance of sustained federal investment in STEM education, workforce development, and research, and I shared how my work supporting the mathematical sciences includes leading federal investments in emerging technologies like artificial intelligence.

It’s always encouraging to see Laredo represented by students helping shape the national conversation on STEM, and contributing to discussions that will influence the future of these critical fields.

Today, I met with Danielle Stewart and Aubrey Wilson from @popvoxfdn to discuss government modernization and the responsible use of AI in public administration.

I’ve spent my career advocating for a government that is more streamlined and accountable, and I’ll keep fighting to codify these reforms so federal agencies are held to clear results. I appreciate the work and partnership of advocates who are helping move this effort forward.

Today, I highlighted several priorities I helped secure in the FY27 Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Appropriations bill during our House Appropriations Committee hearing.

The bill includes language I fought for to support regional task forces focused on cargo theft and supply chain fraud, including $2 million to help protect critical trade routes through the Port of Laredo, which facilitates nearly $340 billion in trade annually, while targeting organized criminal networks tied to drug trafficking and illicit finance.

I also secured provisions to strengthen investigations into dogfighting and cockfighting operations connected to money laundering and other criminal activity. These criminal enterprises threaten our communities, and this bill gives federal law enforcement stronger tools to crack down on them.

The bill advances priorities I fought for to support AI standards and expand practical AI resources for small businesses so South Texas entrepreneurs and local employers can better navigate emerging technologies and remain competitive.

It also provides $84 million for school safety programs, including priorities I secured for rural school districts across South Texas so communities like ours can access stronger mental health resources, prevention programs, and school safety training.

I’ll continue working in a bipartisan way to deliver federal resources, strengthen public safety, protect our economy, and fight for the priorities that matter most to South Texas.

Tell the public what the project will use, protect our water and electricity service, and make the project pay its own cost.

I was honored to participate in the International Catholic Legislators Network’s annual meeting in Rome, where I met with Pope Leo XIV alongside my daughter, Catherine, and heard his address on the challenges and opportunities presented by artificial intelligence.

Pope Leo XIV reminded us that as AI rapidly advances, we must consider not only what technology can do, but what we ought to do. As policymakers, we have a responsibility to ensure AI is developed responsibly, protects human dignity and fundamental freedoms, and serves the common good.

I appreciated the opportunity to hear directly from Pope Leo XIV and engage with Catholic legislators from around the world on this important issue. I’ll continue working to ensure technological innovation serves people, protects our freedoms and strengthens our communities.
Data centers need three things: land, electricity, and water. Rural areas have the land, but ranchers and farmers are very, very worried.

Any of those data centers should pay their way. They should not pass that cost on, whether it's water or electricity. The last thing we want is data centers to pass on the cost of water increases or electricity increases to homeowners, and my bill of rights stops all of that.

This morning, I was pleased to announce $772,700 in FY27 federal funding that I secured through an earmark for TAMIU’s Port Laredo Logistics Ecosystem Project.

The project would establish a Digital Twin and Logistics Resilience Lab at TAMIU’s Western Hemispheric Trade Center, using artificial intelligence, sensors and secure data systems to identify bottlenecks, anticipate disruptions and improve the movement of goods through the Laredo trade corridor.

It would also strengthen Laredo’s role in international trade while creating opportunities for research, innovation and workforce development at TAMIU.

Thank you to TAMIU’s leadership, including Dr. Maynard, Dr. Daniel Covarrubias and Dr. David Salgado, Jerry Maldonado, and the Laredo transportation industry, as well as the faculty and research teams at TAMIU and the Texas A&M Transportation Institute, for their work on this project.

I’ll continue working to bring federal resources back to South Texas that support good jobs, strengthen our economy and build on Laredo’s leadership in international trade.
